title: Session-resilient active-shift protocol for multi-region hosted gateway
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our hosted API gateway must support active-active multi-region traffic shifts while preserving streaming session continuity, meeting SLOs, and avoiding cascading failures. Current failover behavior drops live streaming sessions and often causes KV cache thrashing when traffic shifts quickly across regions. This ticket implements a session-resilient active-shift protocol that coordinates graceful stream handoffs, lightweight KV prefix sync, circuit-breaker policies, and prioritized load-shedding to protect latency and availability SLOs.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic, observable behavior for multi-region active-active traffic shifts with minimal user-visible interruption for both short RPC and long streaming sessions.
- Define & enforce SLOs: availability 99.95% for control-plane operations, p99 non-stream request latency <250ms, streaming continuity (no session drop on region failover) >99.5% for sessions <30 minutes.
- Avoid system-wide congestion by applying circuit breakers and tiered shedding rather than bulk rejects.
- Produce a runbook, metrics dashboard, and automated rollout with canary and auto-rollback.

Scope: Protocol and gateway/controller changes to orchestrate shifts, client-compat knobs (sticky tokens and short-lived session handoff tokens), KV prefix replication for active session metadata, circuit-breaker configuration, load-shedding policy implementation, and observability. Includes conformance tests and a staged rollout.

Out of scope: persistent data migration, private on-prem logic, changes to model runtime internals beyond metrics hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled canary traffic shift from region-a to region-b without manual intervention and with monitored rollback
Streaming session continuity metric shows >=99.5% sessions uninterrupted across a staged 30-minute synthetic load test
No KV hotloop or >20% increase in cross-region KV traffic during steady-state traffic shift
Circuit breakers trip before backend overload and recover automatically per policy with alerting annotated in traces
Observed SLOs: p99 latency <250ms for non-stream requests during normal and staged shift tests, availability >=99.95%
Runbook published with step-by-step rollback and emergency mitigation (rate-limit, global read-only route, disable-shift toggle)
implementation_notes: Introduce 'shift-coordinator' controller that creates per-customer shift plans (traffic weights timeline, session-handoff windows)
Add short-lived HandoffTokens (JWT) issued at gateway to allow session client to reconnect to target region without full re-auth; tokens bound to session id and KV prefix
KV prefix sync: only replicate ephemeral session metadata (prefix per session id) with TTL; implement write-forwarding and lazy prefetch in target region to avoid full KV replication surge

Streaming handoff: orchestrate 3-step handshake: (1) source gate enters DRAIN state for session, signals coordinator; (2) coordinator issues HandoffToken + prefetch request to target; (3) client reconnects to target using token and target streams resume from last-seen message-id via KV checkpoint

Circuit-breaker policy: multi-dimensional (error-rate, p95 latency, CPU utilization) with per-region and per-customer scopes; thresholds: error-rate > 2% over 1m or p95 latency > 500ms => open; exponential backoff probe intervals (30s, 60s, 120s)

Load-shedding: priority queue-based shedding that prefers: (a) shed non-idempotent long-running background requests last, (b) preserve low-cost caching prefixes, (c) fail-fast model fallbacks for heavy token generation requests (switch to lighter model variant), (d) return deterministic 429 with retry-after when shedding
Telemetry: new events session_shift.start/complete/fail, handoff.token_issued, kv.prefetch_hit/miss, cb.open/close, shed.event; hook into SLO dashboards and tracing
Backward compatibility: fall back to existing failover path when coordinator unreachable; ensure client SDK tolerates no-token case by retrying the legacy reconnect flow
Testing: synthetic harness for long-running streams (10k concurrent sessions of 30m each) to measure continuity; chaos tests that simulate region packet loss and controller partition
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary - route 0.5% internal infra traffic with synthetic streams; validate telemetry and KV prefetch patterns
Phase 2: partner beta - enable for selected customers with active support on-call; monitor session continuity and latencies for 48h
Phase 3: gradual ramp - increase to 5%, 25%, 50% over multiple cycles with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
Phase 4: global - enable by default with opt-out knob per-customer; remove opt-out after 90 days if no issues
Emergency rollback: global toggle 'shift-coordinator.disable' to restore legacy single-region failover behavior; immediate rate-limit throttle to 70% if circuit breakers widespread
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for HandoffToken generation/verification and token expiry semantics
Integration test: two-region handshake with KV prefetch accounting and correctness of message-id resume
Load test: 10k concurrent streams, measure failover continuity >=99.5% and extra cross-region bandwidth <20%
Chaos: simulate controller leader partition, verify graceful degradation and fallback route
SLO smoke: scripted calls to assert p99 latency and availability under normal load after each rollout stage
